description: The private messages between the CYFR app's main process and the cyfr program it starts (cyfr desktop-serve): one JSON object a line, on cyfr's stdout (cyfr to main) and its stdin (main to cyfr), each carrying version 2 and its type, and exactly its type's fields. cyfr binds 127.0.0.1:7340 before it sends ready, the chooser's address with the run token in its fragment; as the box's screen (cyfr screen shell) ready is the device's own pages' address, and the same messages follow. home names the CYFR selected, the account service's origin approved for it, its attempt, a whole number from 1, no larger than both sides read exactly, that cyfr gives each proposal of a run, and optionally the SOCKS proxy and resolver rules that reach it, and its road: device, for a CYFR that opens at the device's pages whichever road main offers (one just set up, whose first person is made there), so main loads none of its own pages. Each side honours only its current attempt: main answers the last proposal it read, echoing home and attempt, home-ready once what it keeps is that CYFR's own or home-failed when that could not be, and cyfr takes an answer to the attempt waiting for it alone; an answer to any other changes nothing. home-failed is no lock: that attempt ends unopened. Only after home-ready does cyfr hand a page the CYFR's ticket. home is a proposal until opened, naming the same home and attempt, says cyfr committed it: until then main keeps to none and loads nothing of it, and a lock, a failure or a timeout leaves main able to take cyfr's next home; after it main keeps to that CYFR and takes no other. locked says the device locked, naming the CYFR cyfr holds committed, if any, with home's fields: main destroys its content windows and shows the chooser, and keeps to that CYFR, or none. A lock main begins ends at cyfr's next locked: a home or opened read before it belongs to before the lock and is dropped. main sends lock to lock, leave to lock and let go of the CYFR committed, which cyfr's next locked then names no more (main sends it only once it cleared what it kept of that CYFR), with its id, a whole number from 1, no larger than both sides read exactly, that main gives each departure of a run, and shutdown to end; cyfr answers a leave with left, naming its id, once it let go of that CYFR and ended every session of the device's there, after the locked its lock says: only the left of the departure main waits for ends it, and no locked, nor a left of another id, does; the end of cyfr's stdin ends it too. An end of cyfr sends no locked: main hears the end itself and forgets no sign-in at it. As the box's screen, the shell's last lock, at its end, says ending in place of locked, and the shell says nothing after it: main closes its windows at once and ends, as at cyfr's end, and opens nothing more for it; cyfr desktop-serve says nothing at its end. folder-picked is main's answer to the person's pick of a folder, the chooser's Change…, which main takes as a press and answers by asking the system: its path is the folder, spelled from a root on any system the app runs on (/, a drive's letter, a colon and a separator, or a share's two backslashes), or null where the person cancelled or the pick ended unanswered (the chooser left, its window closed, or a lock), and its epoch and pick, whole numbers from 0 no larger than both sides read exactly, which the chooser's address for the pick named: the time since a lock the chooser was shown in and the picks cyfr had answered before it; cyfr takes only the answer to the pick it would answer now, and one from before a lock or one answered already changes nothing; main sends one for each pick and none otherwise, and nothing else names a folder. external_pages are the pages the chooser may link to, Docker's own pages on installing it: main opens one in the person's browser on a press of the chooser's link, never in the app's window, and opens no other. account_services is the rule both sides hold a home's account service to: https, or plain http for a local CYFR alone (http://localhost, with its port) and only at exactly that CYFR's own origin, each origin in its one spelling: no default port, no leading zero in a port and none past 65535. A line that is not one object, lacks version or carries another, names a type its reader does not read, or has a field missing, unknown or of the wrong kind is refused with the reason named, by the side named in to.
